chapter: New York choir and Rae Harrison
title: Manager Eddie Duisberg warns him to leave Europe
summary: Duisberg told him the political situation would bar him from Berlin, and they later reunited in Majorca.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: There was one thing that we skipped. Was when you came back from Europe in 19 -- was it late '31 or early '32.
You had told me a long time ago that there was a gentleman over there, a German, who sort of advised you to leave Europe. And he knew more, politically, what was
Well, that was Eddie Duseberg, my manager.

Yeah. He said, 'Look here, Sam, you're not going to work in Berlin next year.' And I said, 'At the Hauskomminia (unintelligible).' And he said, 'Because the political situation won't allow you.' He had to be careful how he talked, see. 'They won't allow you to do that right now. And so if I was you, I would leave Europe altogether.' Well, he started me to thinking. And then when it showed up that I couldn't go to London for the six months in the Savoy Hotel, well there wasn't nothing to do but -- that closed the deal. With the wife in pregnancy and the child was born in February. That same February, see, and this was around in December. So. And I found the thing was there was nothing to do but just close the book. And start life over.
So, and then you later ran into him, didn't you?
Yes. He come in when we was playing saloon in (PALMA MIRROCA) Tito's, (unintelligible). He come in there and we fell on each other's shoulders and we cried and had a wonderful time, you know.
It was like old times, you know?
And that was long after the war, right?

Yeah. Eddie and I were just like this, We planned together, you know? We fought together. We went out and socialized together. And we had sex together. We had a wonderful time over there, you know. My wife couldn't stand him because she knew we was running around together. My first wife, not the wife I've got now.
